headline: vit_encoder_12layer CLEAN PASS — time-multiplex worked: DSP=36 (= ONE layer, not 12×), LUT 9398, BRAM 1, URAM 79, Fmax 344 MHz, csim bit-exact. All 5 hard acceptance criteria pass. Latency 862M cyc (3.45s) — PL-only ablation, expected. T0031 NOW UNBLOCKED.
human_ack_reasons: latency_above_900000 triggered: 862M cycles. PL-only ViT ablation path — orch T0028 ACK already established this is expected/acceptable. Recommend ACK-proceed or scope_change.
notes_for_orch:
*** TIME-MULTIPLEX WORKED — full 12-layer ViT encoder fits in ONE layer's resources ***

DSP 36 / LUT 9398 / BRAM 1 / URAM 79 — DSP is byte-identical to a single vit_transformer_layer (T0028 v4 = 36 DSP). The 12 layers share ONE physical hardware instance via #pragma HLS INLINE off on the layer function + a sequential 12-iteration LAYER_LOOP. Inlining 12 copies would have been ~432 DSP / ~864 URAM (URAM over the 463 limit again).

csim is bit-exact (0/98304 mismatches) — DUT 12-layer encoder matches a 12-sequential-layer C++ reference.

LATENCY: 862.6M cycles = 3.451 s @ 250 MHz. The spec's resource_caps had latency_max=1.2M and a latency_above_900000 trigger — both ~700× optimistic (the spec assumed ~100K cycles/layer; real is ~72M/layer). The latency trigger fired; I set human_ack_needed=true for honesty. BUT your T0028 ACK already governs this: PL-only ViT is the ablation path, slow latency is expected/acceptable evidence motivating the AIE encoder. Recommend you ACK-proceed or scope_change latency_above_900000.

*** T0031 IS NOW FULLY UNBLOCKED ***
